question: Between the years of 1950 and 1990, in which year did U.S personal saving rates (measured as household saving as a percent of after-tax income) peak?
raw_response:
I can see the Personal Saving chart clearly. The line peaks at its highest point — reaching about 9.3-9.4 — right between 1970 and 1975, closer to the midpoint/just before 1975. The highest peak is slightly to the left of the 1975 tick mark, around 1973-1974.

Looking carefully, the absolute highest point of the line sits between 1970 and 1975, just left of the 1975 mark. The tick marks are at 5-year intervals (1950, 1955, 1960...). The peak appears at roughly the 1973 position. This corresponds to the well-known historical fact that the U.S. personal saving rate peaked in 1973.

<FINAL_ANSWER>1973</FINAL_ANSWER>
